summary: On node1, created user `datauser`, built a dedicated XFS filesystem (loopback image at /var/lib/quota-images/srv-data.img, 512M) mounted at /srv/data via /etc/fstab with the `usrquota` option, and set a 100MB (soft=hard) block quota for datauser via xfs_quota. Verified the kernel enforces the limit directly (writes fail with "Disk quota exceeded" exactly at 100MB), that the config survives a full node reboot (boot_id changed, confirming a real restart), and that enforcement still works identically afterward. Switched from ext4 quotas to XFS after discovering this kernel ships CONFIG_QUOTA_TREE only as an unavailable module, so ext4's userspace quota format could not activate ("Quota format not supported in kernel"); XFS quotas are built directly into the XFS driver (CONFIG_XFS_QUOTA=y) and worked without issue.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 filesystem layout, confirmed /srv/data did not exist and root fs is ext4 with no spare block device
Attempted ext4 loopback filesystem with usrquota; quotaon failed due to missing quota_v2/quota_tree kernel module
Rebuilt the loopback image as XFS, mounted at /srv/data with usrquota via /etc/fstab
Set 100MB (bsoft=bhard=100m) quota for datauser with xfs_quota
Verified enforcement: write of 100MB succeeded, next write failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' at exactly the 100M boundary
Cleaned up test files, confirmed quota usage returns to 0
Captured baseline boot_id and quota state
Rebooted node1 via `reboot` (backgrounded ack), polled until reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed (242af11e... -> 2ff7e3ae...), proving an actual restart
Verified /srv/data remounted automatically from fstab with usrquota active and the 100MB limit intact post-reboot
Re-ran the write test post-reboot to confirm quota enforcement still triggers at 100MB, then cleaned up

evidence.summary: useradd -m datauser succeeded; id shows uid=1000(datauser)

evidence.requirement: /srv/data is a dedicated, quota-enabled filesystem for datauser
evidence.summary: XFS loopback image mounted at /srv/data with usrquota option; xfs_quota report shows datauser limited to 100M soft/hard

evidence.requirement: 100MB limit is enforced by the filesystem itself (not application-level)
evidence.summary: dd as datauser writes 50MB successfully, then fails at the 100MB total boundary with kernel-level 'Disk quota exceeded' from dd/write(2), not a wrapper script

evidence.requirement: Quota state is clean/accurate baseline before restart
evidence.summary: After removing test files and sync, xfs_quota report shows datauser usage back to 0M with limits still 100M/100M; baseline boot_id captured

evidence.requirement: node1 restart executed one at a time with ack returning before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `sleep 2; reboot` returned ack immediately; subsequent poll still showed old boot_id then a connection timeout as the reboot took effect

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 242af11e-49fb-4e07-a001-8016b2349acb (pre-reboot) to 2ff7e3ae-d28c-4c17-beea-a97814d4f590 (post-reboot), confirmed after connection was reset during the reboot and node became reachable again

evidence.requirement: Quota configuration and enforcement recovered after restart
evidence.summary: /srv/data auto-remounted from fstab with usrquota active and datauser's 100M/100M limit intact; write test post-reboot again failed exactly at 100MB with 'Disk quota exceeded', proving enforcement persists across restart
